issues.legal_issue: A family manager’s sale of ancestral property to meet substantial family debts and benefit the estate remains binding on minor family members despite a small unaccounted portion of the price when the price is not grossly inadequate.
material_facts: An adult son acting as manager of the family sold four of ten mortgaged items of ancestral land after his father’s death, when his two brothers were minors.
Most of the sale price discharged amounts due under mortgages made by the father and a further mortgage made by the adult son; a small balance was paid in cash and was not fully accounted for.
The sale released the six unsold items from the mortgages and relieved the family of rent payable to the mortgagee.
The lower courts valued the sold land at about Rs. 4,000, while the sale price was about Rs. 3,000; the Supreme Court held that price was not grossly inadequate.
There had been continuous dealings between the family and the purchaser’s family over a long period.
issues.conclusion: The sale was binding on the minor family members, and their suit was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A manager’s sale of ancestral property to discharge the father’s debts may be sustained where the bulk of the price is applied to that purpose; a small unaccounted portion does not invalidate the sale if the purchaser acted honestly, family necessity is established, and the price is not unreasonably low. The Court relied on Gauri Shankar v. Jiwan Singh, Niamat Rai v. Din Dayal, Ram Sunder Lal v. Lachhmi Narain, Hanooman Persaud Pandey v. Mt. Babooee Munrai Koonweree, and Radhakrishendas v. Kaluram. It distinguished Balmukand v. Kamla Wati, where the proposed sale was neither to discharge antecedent debts nor to benefit the estate.

rule.if: challenge_to_family_property_sale and ancestral_property_sold_by_family_manager and substantial_family_debts_discharged_from_sale_price and estate_burdens_reduced_by_sale and price_not_grossly_inadequate and small_part_of_price_unaccounted

predicates.challenge_to_family_property_sale: Minor family members challenged a family manager’s sale of ancestral property as not binding on them.
predicates.ancestral_property_sold_by_family_manage: A family manager sold ancestral property on behalf of the family.
predicates.substantial_family_debts_discharged_from: Most of the sale price was applied to discharge debts incurred by the father or family.
predicates.estate_burdens_reduced_by_sale: The sale released other family property from security or otherwise reduced burdens on the estate.
predicates.price_not_grossly_inadequate: The sale price was not unreasonably low in relation to the value of the property sold.
predicates.small_part_of_price_unaccounted: A small portion of the sale price was not shown to have been applied to family debts or another family purpose.

issues.definition: When minor family members challenge a family manager’s sale, the sale remains binding if substantial family debts were discharged, the estate’s burdens were reduced, the price was not grossly inadequate, and only a small part of the price was unaccounted for.

issues.legal_issue: A mortgagee who purchases family property and applies most of the price to discharge the mortgage debts need not separately inquire into whether pressure on the estate justified the sale.
material_facts: The purchaser was the mortgagee under the earlier mortgages over the family land.
Most of the sale price discharged amounts due under the mortgages, and the sale released other mortgaged items from the burden.
The lower courts treated the purchaser’s failure to establish an inquiry into pressure on the estate as a reason to reject the sale.
issues.conclusion: No separate inquiry into pressure on the estate was required in these circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: Where the mortgagee is the purchaser and the greater portion of the sale consideration discharges the mortgage debts, an inquiry into pressure on the estate does not arise. This conclusion is consistent with the principles applied in Gauri Shankar v. Jiwan Singh, Niamat Rai v. Din Dayal, Ram Sunder Lal v. Lachhmi Narain, Hanooman Persaud Pandey v. Mt. Babooee Munrai Koonweree, and Radhakrishendas v. Kaluram.

predicates.challenge_to_family_property_sale: Family members challenged a sale of family property as not binding on them.
predicates.purchaser_is_mortgagee: The purchaser already held a mortgage over the property being sold.
predicates.most_sale_proceeds_discharge_mortgage_de: Most of the sale price was used to discharge mortgage debts owed to the purchaser.

issues.definition: When family members challenge a sale to the mortgagee and most of the price discharges mortgage debts, the purchaser need not inquire into pressure on the estate.
